clinician.trajectory_summary: A 6-year-old patient presented with sudden severe vision loss in the right eye (BCVA 0.02) following blunt ocular trauma. Anterior segment examination revealed hyphema, corneal edema, post-traumatic uveitis, and diminished red reflex. Indirect fundoscopy on admission identified a full-thickness macular rupture, which was confirmed by OCT imaging. The rupture remained stable on follow-up OCT at 2 months with unchanged BCVA. At 3 months post-injury, the patient underwent surgical repair with pars plana vitrectomy (PPV), internal limiting membrane (ILM) peeling using the inverted flap technique, and 20% SF6 gas tamponade. Post-operative OCT at 3 months showed closure of the macular defect with residual tissue reorganization, and BCVA improved to 0.3.
